# FDG5046

> DO use the same name for constructor parameters and a property if the constructor parameters are used just to set the property.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.3 Constructor Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5046
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Name the parameter '{0}' like the property '{1}' that it sets

FDG5046 reports a parameter of an externally visible constructor that is used only to set a property of the instance, through `P = p;`, `this.P = p;` or `P = p ?? throw ...;` in the constructor or, for a primary constructor, through a property initializer `= p`, when the names differ in more than casing. Uses inside nameof do not count. Parameters that set a field are not checked. Renaming a public parameter breaks callers that use named arguments, so there is no code fix.

## From the book

The only difference between such parameters and the properties should be casing.

```csharp
public class EventLog {
  public EventLog(string logName){
    this.LogName = logName;
  }
  public string LogName {
    get { ... }
    set { ... }
  }
}
```
